messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated packet loss observed for egress to eu-west-1 via ProviderZ. Automatic health checks show 30-40% packet loss for ALB egress paths from 03:12-03:15 UTC. Paging on-call.

katie (on-call): acked. I'm taking this. any immediate customer pages?

ops-bot: paging: @katie (on-call)

katie (on-call): quick check — are we seeing DNS failures or TCP retries upstream?

dave-net: I see heavy loss on a specific upstream ASN (AS64567) across multiple peering sessions. Likely a partial hardware issue on ProviderZ peering fabric. Traceroute drops at provider transit hop.

dave-net: attaching quick traceroute sample:
```
traceroute to 54.239.XX.XX (54.239.XX.XX), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  internal-gw (10.0.0.1)  0.3 ms  0.2 ms  0.2 ms
 2  providerz-peering (198.51.100.5)  5.2 ms  8.3 ms  1200 ms  <-- intermittent high latency/loss
 3  providerz-core (198.51.100.1)  * * *
 4  cloud-eu (54.239.XX.XX)  14.5 ms  14.5 ms  14.7 ms
```

sofia-product: customers in eu-west-1 are reporting slow API responses and a couple of support tickets. We got a banner from status that some customers see elevated latencies. No full region outage.

katie (on-call): Maria — can you confirm if healthcheck retries triggered failover to secondary egress? I believe we have a fallback policy to prefer ProviderY when loss > 20%.

maria-sre: The automatic routing fallback didn't fully trigger because sessions remained UP from BGP perspective, loss was observed at data-plane only. BGP state remained stable so no RIB change. We're at an edge case: data-plane degraded but control-plane ok.

dave-net: Plan: 1) steer new outbound sessions to ProviderY via BGP local-preference for critical prefixes, 2) request ProviderZ NOC for immediate investigation with sample pcap/traceroute, 3) lower DNS TTL for affected hostnames to 30s to accelerate client flipover to other IPs behind alternate egress.

katie (on-call): I'll start the steering. Changing local-pref for 54.239.0.0/16 to prefer ProviderY for production-ASNs. Doing a canary shift to 5% first.

dave-net: ETA 2m for canary announcement. applying route-map now.

katie (on-call): applied. canary 5% traffic shifted via ProviderY. Monitoring metrics.

ops-bot: metric update: packet loss for path via ProviderZ down from 38% -> 26% after canary, latency still spiky.

raj (oncall-2): I'm on standby for handoff in 20m. If this persists past the hour we should rotate oncall.

sofia-product: Coordinating with CS: advising customers about increased latency and that we are actively steering traffic and working with provider. Using emergency banner: "Degraded egress to eu-west-1 via one upstream provider; mitigation in progress". :information_source:

dave-net: ProviderZ NOC contacted (ticket #PZ-8791). They asked for pcap from our egress host. Preparing capture now.

katie (on-call): please run tcpdump on egress host 10.200.5.12 port 443 for 60s and upload to secure bucket. Use this command:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 54.239.XX.XX and port 443 -w /tmp/pz-egress.pcap -c 10000
```

maria-sre: Captured and uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-pcaps/1767012345/pz-egress.pcap. Sent to ProviderZ NOC with traceroute logs. They responded: "packet discard observed on our edge, investigating ASIC errata".

ops-bot: note: automatic failover threshold at 20% loss requires confirmed BGP withdraw, which didn't occur. Manual steering executed as above.

katie (on-call): After manual steering to ProviderY at 5% then 20% then 70% the application latency for affected customers is back to baseline. Will keep ProviderZ traffic limited to 10% while they investigate.

sofia-product: CS updated customers and closed 3 urgent tickets with workaround info. We set support priority to P1 for any new regressions.

dave-net: Next steps: 1) keep ProviderZ at reduced traffic, 2) collect more pcaps and BGP counters, 3) if ProviderZ reports hardware replacement complete, gradually move traffic back and run soak tests.

raj (oncall-2): Handoff note for next oncall: restored baseline for now, ProviderZ under investigation (ticket PZ-8791). If packet loss resurfaces, escalate to network leadership and consider multi-CDN for critical endpoints.

katie (on-call): handing off to @raj in 15m. I'll remain available for any immediate follow-ups. Logging postmortem checklist in #postmortems.

maria-sre: adding incident record: impact: increased latency/packet loss for eu-west-1 outbound, affected ~12% of API requests for 22m window, mitigation: manual egress steering to ProviderY. Tags: networking, egress, providerz, mitigation.

ops-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. :white_check_mark:

katie (on-call): thanks team. I'll draft initial incident summary and timeline and post to #postmortems once handoff complete. :thumbsup:
